newsitem.title: UK: British minister resigns over sleaze probe-agency.
newsitem.headline: British minister resigns over sleaze probe-agency.

text.p: A junior minister in the British Treasury, David Willetts, said on Wednesday he would resign as a minister after being strongly criticised by fellow members of parliament investigating allegations of so-called "sleaze".
Prime Minister John Major's office said Willetts, 40, had tendered his resignation as Paymaster-General. Willetts was a key strategist in Major's administration and was tipped for high office.
His resignation came within minutes of the parliamentary Standards and Privileges Committee saying it could not accept Willetts' evidence to the committee had been "accurate".

The report followed a two-month inquiry into Willetts' role in a row over allegations a former minister took cash and favours in return for asking parliamentary questions on behalf of Mohammed Al Fayed, the owner of London's top store, Harrods.

The committee was investigating whether Willetts, when he was a "whip" or government business manager, improperly tried to influence another panel of members of parliament probing the former minister Neil Hamilton.
